algorithm: Periodic sampling with static threshold evaluation

classes.desc: Samples metrics, evaluates thresholds, and collects alerts.
classes.name: Monitor

data_flow_ascii:
seeded RNG -> read_metrics (cpu, memory, latency)
reading -> check_thresholds -> alert strings
Monitor.run: sample, print, alert, sleep -> summary
description_sentence: Samples synthetic topic metrics for N cycles, evaluates each reading against thresholds, prints readings and alerts.
failure_note: A reading exactly at the threshold does not alert (strictly-greater comparison); with zero cycles the run prints only the summary line.

functions.desc: Sample one synthetic topic metric reading.
functions.name: read_metrics

functions.desc: Return a list of alert strings for readings over threshold.
functions.name: check_thresholds

functions.desc: Sample `cycles` readings, print them, return alert count.
functions.name: Monitor.run

functions.desc: Parse args and run the monitor.
functions.name: main

label: Monitoring agent
output_shape: One line per cycle (cpu, memory, latency) with ALERT lines for threshold breaches, plus a cycle/alert summary.
pitch_sentence: A {topic} monitoring agent in pure Python that samples synthetic metrics on a cadence, checks them against thresholds, and reports every breach.

qa.a: From PARAMS thresholds, overridable per template instance; defaults are 85% CPU, 90% memory, 500ms latency.
The RNG is seeded, so the same seed replays the same readings and alerts for debugging.
Yes, but it would be single-process and in-memory, so it fits demos and prototypes rather than fleet monitoring.

resume_bullet_template: Built a {topic} monitoring agent in Python (stdlib) sampling synthetic CPU, memory, and latency metrics on a fixed cadence; evaluates threshold breaches and prints readings with alerts and a summary.
scaling_note: Single-process in-memory sampling; real fleet monitoring would need persistence, alerting integrations, and horizontal collectors.
storage_note: In-memory only: readings and alerts are printed to stdout and kept in a list for the run summary; nothing is persisted.
tradeoff_note: Synthetic seeded metrics keep the demo self-contained and deterministic, at the cost of not observing any real system.
